title: MVNEX | Sebastian Sanchez
description: Case study for MVNEX, a systems project in C++ focused on performance, data structures, and implementation depth.
ogDescription: A C++ systems project focused on performance, data structures, and technical depth.
name: MVNEX
headline: A project for moving lower in the stack, thinking about performance, and strengthening fundamentals.
summary: MVNEX is a C++ project focused on practicing data structures, algorithms, performance, and lower-level design. It is not meant to be a commercial product; it is a space for building technical judgment outside the comfort of web frameworks.

problem.title: Starting point
problem.body: Modern development often helps us move fast, but it can also hide how software actually behaves. MVNEX exists to practice decisions closer to the system: structures, memory, execution costs, and internal design.
points: Step outside the usual framework workflow and work with C++.
Practice Computer Science fundamentals in real code.
Understand tradeoffs between simplicity, performance, and control.

role.title: My role
role.body: This is a personal project, so my role covers design, implementation, manual testing, internal decisions, and documenting the learning. The goal is to improve judgment, not just finish features.

sections.title: Why it exists
sections.body: Not all of my learning lives inside web frameworks. MVNEX exists to force slower and more precise thinking about how code is organized and executed.
points: Practice data structures from an implementation-oriented perspective.
Understand how small decisions affect performance and clarity.
Strengthen fundamentals that also improve my backend and architecture work.

sections.title: What it explores
sections.body: The project focuses on C++, data structures, algorithms, internal API design, and development habits closer to systems work.
points: Data structures with attention to cost and behavior.
Reading code through maintainability, not only whether it works.
Work with Linux, Git, and more manual testing cycles.

sections.title: Challenges
sections.body: Unlike a web app, feedback here is not always visual. The challenge is to reason better, measure when needed, and avoid hiding complexity behind premature abstractions.
points: Avoid building abstractions before understanding the problem.
Keep code readable while optimizing concrete parts.
Distinguish between real performance work and micro-optimizations with no impact.
Document decisions so the project does not become a black box.

sections.title: What I want to learn
sections.body: I want to improve my judgment for writing efficient software, understanding performance tradeoffs, and connecting Computer Science fundamentals with real code.
points: Think better about memory, structures, and complexity.
Write code that is more explicit and easier to reason about.
Bring algorithms and design fundamentals into practical decisions.
Improve my instinct for knowing when a simple solution is already enough.

next.title: Next
next.body: Keep iterating on the internal design, add clearer usage examples, and turn the most important lessons into more specific technical notes.
